source.title: The Number of Weak Characters in the Game

teaching.hint: After ordering by one property, what must happen to equal-valued groups?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Sort by attack to turn two-dimensional dominance into a defense maximum scan; equal-attack entries must be prevented from dominating one another.
solution_outline.approach: Sort by descending attack, breaking equal-attack ties by ascending defense. Scan in that order and count a character when an earlier defense maximum is strictly larger.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: At a character, any earlier equal-attack entry has defense no larger than its defense, so a larger stored maximum must come from a strictly higher-attack entry.
solution_outline.correctness: The stored maximum witnesses weakness exactly when it exceeds the current defense. Later entries have no greater attack, so no missed dominator can appear later.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(n log n)` time for sorting and `O(1)` additional scan state, excluding sort workspace.
solution_outline.pitfall: Descending defense within equal attack values falsely counts lower-defense peers as weak.

common_wrong_turns: Letting same-attack characters dominate one another
source_fidelity_notes: Removed examples; retained both strict inequalities and duplicate-property possibilities.
